name: Call Telegram Bot API method
description: Calls any Telegram Bot API method through one of the venue's bots, with the method's own parameters exactly as documented at https://core.telegram.org/bots/api, and returns Telegram's result. This is how everything beyond plain text is done: sendPhoto / sendDocument / sendVoice / sendMediaGroup (media by file_id, URL, or multipart files containing protected content references), editMessageText, deleteMessage, answerCallbackQuery, sendChatAction, getChat, setMessageReaction, getFile, ... Maps and arrays in params are sent as JSON as Telegram expects. Refused: getUpdates, setWebhook, deleteWebhook, logOut, close (the venue's own update loop owns them). On an allow-listed bot every chat_id, from_chat_id and user_id in params must be an allowed user — a numeric id on its allow list, or the account a listed @username resolved to when that person first wrote; the bot only messages its allowed users. Methods that address no chat or user (answerCallbackQuery, ...) pass. Requires telegram/call on <bot user>/telegram/<bot> — a broader ability than telegram/send.

bot.description: Bot name (adapters.telegram.bots key). Optional when the caller owns exactly one bot.

method.description: Bot API method name, e.g. sendPhoto, editMessageText, answerCallbackQuery

params.description: The method's parameters as documented by Telegram (snake_case), e.g. {"chat_id": 123, "photo": "https://...", "caption": "..."}

files.description: Multipart file parts, each {ref, filename?}. References resolve under the caller's authority, max 20 MiB total and 10 parts per call. For one file use files.photo and omit params.photo. For albums use params.media entries with media attach://partName and files.partName.

output.description: Telegram's result for the method: a Message for send*/edit* methods, true for most others, or the documented object (Chat, File, ...).
